claims.claim: A traction elevator counterweight = empty car weight + 40-50% of the rated load (the 'overbalance').
sources: https://elevatorworld.com/article/deadweight-dead-wrong/ (Elevator World: 40-42.5% traditionally, 45-50% on newer PM gearless)

claims.claim: The machine only lifts/holds the unbalance (difference); full car = car side heavier, empty car = counterweight side heavier.
With an empty car, a released brake would let the car rise and the counterweight fall.
sources: https://hsmuniversity.org/us/course/elv-230-traction-elevators-machines-and-ropes/lesson-4-counterweight-balance-and-compensation (empty car: counterweight side heavier by kQ)

note: Bars in the video use the HSM worked example (car 3,300 lb, rated 3,500 lb, 45% overbalance, CW 4,875 lb). Applies to traction elevators, not hydraulic ones.
